## Today's Agenda

*Everything you need to hit the ground running in AI 380.*

1. **Course at a glance** — what this course is about, and who it's for
2. **Logistics** — meeting times, location, instructor, communication
3. **The 15-week journey** — four modules, from HCI foundations to a live conversational AI
4. **Grading & assignments** — how your grade is built, week by week
5. **The group project** — two sequential projects worth 40% of your grade
6. **Policies** — attendance, late work, AI use, and academic honesty

## Course at a Glance

**Human-AI Interaction · Designing Intelligent Systems that Work for Humans**

This course introduces the core principles of human-centered design for conversational AI systems — chatbots, virtual assistants, and interactive voice interfaces. You'll explore how NLP, dialogue management, and UX principles converge to create intuitive, accessible, and inclusive AI interactions.

::: {.callout}
"Designing AI that works for humans — in all their wonderful diversity."
:::

| | |
|---|---|
| **4 credit hours** | ≈ 6–9 hrs/week outside class |
| **Prerequisite: CS 151** | Non-CS majors warmly welcome |
| **Group project** | 2–3 members, worth 40% of grade |

## Who Is This Course For?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Prerequisite**

CS 151 is required before taking this course. Prior software engineering experience is a plus, but not required.

**Interdisciplinary by design**

Non-CS majors are strongly encouraged to enroll — diverse perspectives are essential for designing AI systems that work for everyone.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Group project commitment**

This course requires substantial group work across the semester. Be ready to collaborate in teams of 2–3 on a full design and evaluation project.

**Our value statement**

We are committed to an equitable, inclusive, and welcoming learning environment.
:::
:::

## Course Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, you will be able to...

**01 — Critique & Synthesize Research**
Review scientific literature in human-AI interaction to synthesize trends and inform evidence-based design decisions.

**02 — Design Conversational Systems**
Apply human-centered design alongside NLP and dialogue management to prototype functional, context-aware conversational interfaces.

**03 — Evaluate Usability & Ethics**
Conduct rigorous usability testing to assess user trust, efficiency, and error recovery, while analyzing ethical risks.

**04 — Collaborate & Communicate**
Work in multidisciplinary teams to manage interactive AI projects, communicating outcomes professionally.

## Module 1 · Human-AI Interaction & User-Centered Design {.smaller}

*Weeks 1–4 · Aug 24 – Sep 16 · Foundations of HCI, role of humans in AI, design thinking, needfinding, personas.*

| Week | Focus | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kick-off + HAI Roots | Introduction & The Role of Humans in AI |
| 2 | History & Reality | Historical Perspective & Everyday AI |
| 3 | Research Methods | Understanding Users & Personas |
| 4 | Design Thinking | Design Process & Workshop 1 |

**Key readings:** Amershi et al. "Power to the People" (AI Magazine) · Dijkstra "On the Foolishness of Natural Language Programming" · Shneiderman & Maes "Direct Manipulation vs. Interface Agents"

## Module 2 · Human-AI Collaborations {.smaller}

*Weeks 5–8 · Sep 21 – Oct 14 · Conversational AI design, HAI challenges, dialogue guidelines, Lab 1, Workshop 2, midterm quiz.*

| Week | Focus | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Conversational AI | The Conversational Agent Paradigm & Lab 1 |
| 6 | Challenges & Guidelines | HAI Challenges & Microsoft's 18 Guidelines |
| 7 | CALM + Assessment | Conversational AI (Part 1) & Midterm Quiz |
| 8 | Patterns + Workshop | Designing for Success & Workshop 2 |

**Key readings:** Cai et al. "Re-examining Whether, Why, and How HAI Is Uniquely Difficult" · Amershi et al. "Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction" (CHI 2019) · Luger & Sellen "Like Having a Really Bad PA"

## Module 3 · AI Design & Conversational Orchestration {.smaller background-color="#003B5C"}

*Weeks 9–11 · Oct 19 – Nov 4 · Deep-dive into building AI assistants with Rasa CALM.*

| Week | Focus | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | CALM Architecture | CALM & Lab 2 |
| 10 | NLU + Debugging | CALM Overview & Lab 3 |
| 11 | Accessibility + QA | Building for Success & Lab 4 |

**Key reading:** Rasa Documentation — CALM Overview, Actions & Custom Actions, Deployment & Channels

## Module 4 · UX, Usability Study, Report & Presentation {.smaller}

*Weeks 12–15 · Nov 9 – Dec 2 · Usability testing with real older adults, heuristic evaluation, final presentations.*

| Week | Focus | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | Evaluation Methods | Testing & Heuristic Evaluation |
| 13 | Field Results | Interface Testing & Documentation |
| 14 | Peer Review | Future Tech & Peer Review |
| 15 | Showcase | Final Project Presentations |

**Key readings:** Nielsen "How to Conduct a Heuristic Evaluation" · "Ethics Pathways in HCI Research" · Eagleman "Can We Create New Senses for Humans?" (TED)

## Course Structure & Assessment {background-color="#BA0C2F"}

Five components make up how you'll learn — and how you'll be graded.

1. **Lectures** — Every Mon & Wed, Aug 24 – Dec 4. Attendance and participation are mandatory and graded.
2. **Weekly Readings & Homework** — Individual readings, 3–4 homework assignments, one short individual project.
3. **Group Project** — Two major group projects, from need-finding through usability evaluation.
4. **Mid-term Quiz** — Week 7 in-class quiz testing Modules 1–2 content.
5. **Final Reflection Essay** — Individual essay connecting learning outcomes to broader AI design themes.

## Project 1: VR Learning Environment {.smaller}

*Co-designing and authoring a 9-screen VR intervention for older adults, validated on the Meta Quest 3.*

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Design Considerations for Older Adults (70+)**

- Large UI targets — generous touch/pointer areas
- High-contrast visual cues that remain legible
- Gentle pacing — no time pressure
- Audio support — instructions read aloud
- Low-stress error recovery — no penalties
- Minimal cognitive load — one action per screen
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Example: Medication Management**

1. Why Medication Schedules Matter
2. Inspect the Pill Bottle
3. Food vs. Empty Stomach
4. Morning Routine Steps
5. Emergency Kit Checklist
6. Key Terms & Definitions
7. Storage Best Practices
8. Handling Missed Doses
9. Reminder Alarm Logic
:::
:::

## Project 2: Conversational AI Assistants

*Guided by Design Thinking, teams work with older adults across the full semester.*

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Cognitive Enhancement**

Memory support, medication reminders, cognitive exercises
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Physical Mobility Support**

Navigation assistance, exercise guidance, fall-risk awareness
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Social Well-Being**

Companionship interfaces, family communication, social activities
:::
:::

::: {.callout}
**Tech stack for GP3:** Rasa CALM (or equivalent) for multi-turn dialogue · Docker for full-stack containerization · Accessible web/mobile UI with high-contrast, speech-to-text support.
:::

## Course Policies {background-color="#BA0C2F"}

::: {.kicker}
PROFESSIONALISM & INTEGRITY
:::

Attendance, late work, generative AI use, and academic honesty — know these before Week 1.

## Attendance & Late Submission

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Attendance & Participation**

- Attend all classes, labs, and workshops — come prepared to contribute meaningfully.
- Attendance is tracked randomly through in-class participation activities.
- Participation activities cannot be made up if missed.
- Unable to attend? Notify the instructor as soon as possible.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Late Submission: Not Allowed Without Approval**

- Email the instructor before the deadline explaining the situation.
- Receive a written reply confirming any extension.
- No lateness beyond 24 hours is tolerated without explicit approval.
- Maximum of 2 late submissions allowed across the entire course.
:::
:::

## Policy on AI & Generative AI Use {background-color="#003B5C"}

*This course heavily integrates AI — use it responsibly, and always disclose it.*

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**AI is encouraged for...**

- Explaining complex concepts
- Providing coding examples
- Offering debugging suggestions
- Recommending best practices
- Exploring new ideas and approaches

**Responsible use requires:** never using AI to solve entire assignments, always acknowledging AI usage, understanding everything you submit.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**The perils of over-reliance**

- **Hinders your learning** — hands-on problem-solving is irreplaceable
- **Impedes your growth** — prevents critical thinking development
- **Limits your creativity** — over-dependence stifles innovation
- **Compromises your career** — employers value independent thinkers
:::
:::

## Academic Honesty for CS Students {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.tag-field}
**Reasonable**

- Talking with classmates about assignments
- Discussing strategies verbally (no code shared)
- Whiteboarding a solution together
- Searching the web for general concepts
- Small cited code snippets
- Working with a tutor on your own code
:::
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.tag-gold}
**Careful**

- Showing code to another student for debugging only, in private
- Reviewing others' code after submission to enhance learning
:::
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.tag-cardinal}
**Not Reasonable**

- Submitting another's work as your own
- Copying from a quiz or exam
- Viewing or copying another's solution
- Copying solutions from previous years
- Recording or sharing exam content
- Maintaining public repositories of solutions
:::
:::
:::

## Our Value Statement {background-color="#003B5C"}

This course is designed for students from **all disciplinary backgrounds** — not just Computer Science. We believe diverse perspectives are essential for designing AI systems that work for everyone.

Students of different abilities, identities, and disciplinary backgrounds bring unique value to human-centered AI design. Your perspective on how AI systems affect your community is not just welcome — it is essential to the course's intellectual mission.

::: {.callout}
"The goal is not to build AI that thinks like humans, but AI that works for humans — in all their wonderful diversity."
:::
